RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Quinn Grant
Member ID: W331641494
Plan: Dean Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin
Reference Number: POC-5BC8A5312C-11722
Requested Service: Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-10
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-06

To the Grievance and Appeal Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22551 (anterior cervical discectomy and fusion), as set out in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-10. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I disagree with this determination and ask that it be reversed, because the medical record already in the plan's possession documents a conservative-treatment trial that meets the plan's own published criteria.

Based on my research, Dean Health Plan administers prior authorization for cervical spine surgery, including CPT 22551, through Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates/NIA), applying Evolent's clinical guideline for cervical spine surgery. I have located and am quoting below from two versions of that guideline that I was able to retrieve: (1) "Evolent Clinical Guideline 1759 for Cervical Spine Surgery," Guideline Number Evolent_CG_1759, Last Revised December 2025, Implementation Date July 2026 (at https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf); and (2) the prior edition of the same guideline, then numbered NIA_CG_307, Last Revised Date May 2023, Implementation Date January 2024. I have not been able to confirm which exact edition Dean/Evolent applied to my case, and I ask the plan to identify that edition and to apply whichever version's criteria my record satisfies.

I have not been provided the plan's internal review notes, so beyond the quoted guideline language below, the arguments in this letter regarding what "meets" or "does not meet" a given criterion are my own characterization of my record against that language, not a quotation from the plan.

The Evolent_CG_1759 (2026) guideline states, for Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) – Single Level, that surgery is indicated "When ALL of the following criteria are met": "Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity"; "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months; NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment. Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute 'inability to complete' treatment."; and "Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at the level corresponding with the clinical findings."

The earlier NIA_CG_307 (2024) edition of the same guideline set out the conservative-care element in more specific terms: "Persistent or recurrent symptoms/pain with functional limitations that are unresponsive to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative treatment," and "Documented failure of at least 6 consecutive weeks in the last 6 months of any 2 of the following physician-directed conservative treatments: o Analgesics, steroids, and/or NSAIDs o Structured program of physical therapy o Structured home exercise program prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider or physician o Epidural steroid injections and or selective nerve root block."

My record satisfies these criteria under either edition:

1. Cervical radiculopathy from a ruptured disc, corresponding to imaging: MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-07-13 documents a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This is consistent with the guideline's requirement of "cervical radiculopathy ... from ruptured disc" and with the requirement that "imaging studies confirm the presence of ... spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at the level corresponding with the clinical findings." My reported radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger, associated weakness, and positive provocative testing on the affected side correspond directly to a C6 nerve root distribution, matching the imaged level.

2. Conservative treatment trial well in excess of six weeks: I completed a supervised course of physical therapy — including cervical traction and postural training — from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24 (16 completed visits over 16 weeks), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This is more than double the six-consecutive-week minimum referenced in the guideline and falls within the "last six (6) months" window relative to both the imaging study and the denial date. In addition, I was treated with NSAIDs for approximately four months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 that produced only four weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned. Under either edition of the guideline, this represents more than one physician-directed conservative modality (structured physical therapy plus analgesic/anti-inflammatory medication plus an injection) sustained well beyond six weeks.

3. Failure of that conservative treatment as defined by the guideline: My symptoms have been present and progressive for 24 months, are unrelieved by rest, and did not resolve with 16 weeks of physical therapy, four months of NSAIDs, or a corticosteroid injection (which gave only four weeks of partial benefit before recurrence). This is consistent with the guideline's definition of failure of conservative treatment as "lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment" and/or "progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment." There is no indication in my record of any "medical reason [I was] unable to participate in treatment," non-compliance, or missed care due to office closures — to the contrary, the physical therapy discharge note documents that I completed the full prescribed course.

For these reasons, the specific basis stated in the denial notice — that the record does not document "an adequate trial of conservative treatment" — is not supported by the record that was submitted with the prior authorization request, which includes a documented 16-week supervised physical therapy course, a four-month NSAID trial, a corticosteroid injection, and imaging (2026-07-13 MRI) confirming a C5-C6 disc herniation with foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression corresponding to my clinical findings.

I am requesting that Dean Health Plan/Evolent:
1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551 as requested by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti;
2. If the plan maintains the denial, identify in writing the specific guideline title, guideline/policy number, and effective/revision date actually applied to my case, and identify precisely which criterion or element of that guideline my record is found not to satisfy; and
3. Offer my treating surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, a peer-to-peer review with the reviewing physician before any further adverse determination is issued.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note documenting the course of care from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24; records of NSAID therapy and the 2026-04-21 corticosteroid injection; the 2026-07-13 cervical MRI report; and my surgeon's clinical notes documenting exam findings, radicular symptoms, and surgical plan.

I understand that this appeal must be received by 2027-02-06, and I am submitting it well in advance of that deadline. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise me of the expected timeframe for a determination. I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions, and I authorize you to discuss this appeal with my treating surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, at [provider phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Quinn Grant
Member ID: W331641494

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24); medication/injection records; MRI report dated 2026-07-13; surgeon's clinical notes (Dr. Marchetti)
